memories.memory: I still have breakfast with my younger sister every other Saturday, and we are trying to settle an old disagreement about who should keep our mother's cedar hope chest.
After thirty-one years in municipal public works, I was promoted to deputy director in 2018 and found the leadership responsibilities more satisfying than the title itself.
Last November, I had a tense meeting with my supervisor after she credited a major accessibility project to a newer manager, even though I had led the planning and secured the $420,000 budget.
My daughter and her husband live about three hours away, so I help with their two children during school holidays and usually stay in their guest room for four or five nights.
I have been seeing a widower named Martin for nearly two years, but we maintain separate homes because I am not ready to combine finances or give up my routines.
A former coworker, Denise, calls me every Tuesday evening for advice about applying for management positions, and I review her interview answers even when I am tired.
I took six weeks of family leave in 2021 to help my brother recover from knee replacement surgery, and returning to work was difficult because a temporary manager had reorganized my entire team.
